book.title: A Christmas Carol · Stave 1 — Marley's Ghost
book.author: Charles Dickens, A Christmas Carol (1843)

adaptation._text_policy: Retell each beat in clear, lively V-Level-7 English. Keep story beats, characters and a few iconic lines verbatim (by=DICKENS 1843); rewrite dense archaic captions; <=2 text blocks per panel; every SPEECH bubble is spoken by the on-screen character (no off-panel speakers); diegetic signage is NEVER baked into the art (blank in art, correct spelling supplied as HTML caption). retention-band metric retired for the comic tier.
iconic_quotes_kept: I wear the chain I forged in life
You will be haunted by Three Spirits

cast.name: Scrooge
cast.role: protagonist — cold, miserly old man who is redeemed
cast.canonical: a bent thin elderly man, completely bald on top with short wispy grey side-hair, a long smooth clean-shaven bare face, sharp pointed nose, thin hard lips and hollow cheeks, in a shabby dark Victorian tailcoat
cast.anchor: bent thin bald old man, smooth bare clean-shaven face, sharp pointed nose
cast.distinct_from: NOT a ghost — he is solid/opaque, wears NO head-bandage and drags NO chain

cast.name: Marley's Ghost
cast.role: Scrooge's dead partner — a warning spirit
cast.canonical: the see-through translucent ghost of a gaunt stooped old man, a white cloth bandage tied up over the top of his head and under his jaw, a grey pigtail (queue) at the back, an old-fashioned waistcoat and knee-breeches, wound in a long heavy chain hung with cash-boxes, keys, padlocks and ledgers
cast.anchor: translucent gaunt old ghost, jaw-bandage over the head, bound in a chain of cash-boxes and padlocks
cast.distinct_from: unlike Scrooge he is TRANSPARENT, always wears the jaw-bandage and always drags the money-chain; a thin OLD man, never muscular

cast.name: Bob Cratchit
cast.canonical: a thin gentle clerk with dark hair and a mild kind face, wound in a very long white knitted comforter scarf and fingerless mittens, in a threadbare coat with no overcoat
cast.anchor: thin dark-haired clerk, long white comforter scarf, fingerless mittens
cast.distinct_from: NOT bald, wears NO holly — he is not Fred

cast.name: Fred
cast.canonical: a cheerful handsome young man with dark side-whiskers and a small moustache, bright warm eyes, a scarf and a sprig of holly pinned to his coat
cast.anchor: cheerful young man, dark side-whiskers, holly sprig on his coat
cast.distinct_from: young and warm — not the bald old miser

panels.scene: a bleak snowy London churchyard at dusk, bare black trees and a stone church behind, a fresh plain gravestone in the snow; the bent bald pointed-nosed old miser in a long shabby dark tailcoat stands coldly over it, both hands resting on his cane, unmoved
panels.composition: wide, a cold opening at the grave

bubbles.text: Old Marley — Scrooge's business partner — was dead. Dead as a doornail. And Scrooge stood over his grave, unmoved.

panels.scene: a grimy London counting-house doorway in a brick wall, a weathered empty wooden sign-board hanging blank above the door; the bent bald pointed-nosed miser in his shabby dark tailcoat unlocking the door, sour and tight-fisted
panels.composition: close, the miser and his firm

teen.narration: YEARS PASSED. SCROOGE NEVER CHANGED THE NAME.

bubbles.text: The old sign still read SCROOGE AND MARLEY — and it was all the same to him.

panels.scene: a tight close portrait of the bald pointed-nosed old miser, deep frown, sunken glaring eyes and a thin hard mouth drawn in stark black ink, a frosty rime on his brow, radiating cold, in a dark tailcoat
panels.composition: close, the coldest man in London

bubbles.text: A greedy, grasping old sinner — cold to the bone, and colder still to everyone else.

panels.scene: the bald pointed-nosed miser walking a frozen London street at night, snow and wind streaming past while he ignores it entirely, hunched in a long dark coat, a gas-lamp and shuttered shops behind him

bubbles.text: Heat could not warm him; cold could not chill him. The nastiest weather never bothered Scrooge — he was worse.

panels.scene: a cramped dark counting-house on Christmas Eve; the thin dark-haired clerk wound in a very long white knitted comforter scarf and fingerless mittens, hunched and shivering over papers at a tiny desk beside one tiny glowing coal, a frosted foggy window behind

teen.narration: CHRISTMAS EVE. SCROOGE KEPT HIS CLERK, BOB CRATCHIT, IN THE COLD.

bubbles.text: Bob's fire was so small it looked like a single coal — and Scrooge kept the coal-box locked in his own room.

panels.scene: the cheerful young man Fred with dark side-whiskers and a moustache, a scarf and a sprig of holly on his coat, bursting in from the frosty street with both arms wide and a warm grin, cheeks glowing, an office doorway behind him

teen.narration: THEN HIS CHEERFUL NEPHEW, FRED, BURST IN.

bubbles.speaker: FRED
bubbles.text: A merry Christmas, uncle!

panels.scene: the bald clean-shaven pointed-nosed old miser (smooth chin, no beard) in a dark tailcoat, scowling and jabbing a bony finger, leaning over a big open ledger at his desk, shelves behind

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: Bah! Humbug!

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: What right have YOU to be merry? You're poor enough!

panels.scene: the cheerful young man Fred, dark side-whiskers, moustache, a holly sprig on his coat, speaking warmly with shining eyes and one hand on his heart, a cosy office behind; he is the only person in the picture

bubbles.speaker: FRED
bubbles.text: And what right have you to be so grumpy? You're rich enough!

bubbles.speaker: FRED
bubbles.text: Christmas is the one time we open our hearts and think of others. God bless it!

panels.scene: the bald pointed-nosed miser frowning coldly over papers at his desk, one hand raised flat to refuse, a dim counting-house around him

teen.narration: TWO MEN CAME COLLECTING FOR THE POOR.

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: Are there no prisons? No workhouses?

panels.scene: the cold miser at his cluttered money-desk turning back to his coins and waving one hand dismissively over his shoulder to send the collectors away, a hard sneer on his face, shelves of ledgers and a counting-house window behind him — a full room, not empty space

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: If they would rather die, they had better do it — and decrease the surplus population.
He meant the poor should be shut away in prisons and workhouses — or left to die.

panels.scene: night; the thin dark-haired clerk Bob in his long white comforter scarf runs and slides along a long stripe of ice down the middle of a snowy lane, arms out for balance, grinning, a line of boys sliding behind him under the gas-lamps

teen.narration: SCROOGE GRUMBLED, BUT GAVE BOB CHRISTMAS DAY OFF.

bubbles.text: Bob slid all the way down the icy lane, then ran home to play games with his family.

panels.scene: night, the miser in a coat recoiling at his own front door; the round brass door-knocker has turned into the glowing translucent ghostly face of his dead partner Marley — an old face wrapped in a white bandage tied over the head and under the jaw, dim round spectacles pushed up on the forehead — staring sadly; a dark house door and step around it
panels.composition: close, the knocker becomes a face

teen.narration: THAT NIGHT, AT HIS OWN DOOR…

bubbles.text: The knocker was not a knocker — it was Marley's face. Then, in a blink, it was a knocker again.

panels.scene: the miser in a striped nightgown and floppy nightcap starting up from a chair beside a low fire as a big old bell high on the wall swings wildly by itself with motion lines, dread on his face, a dim room

teen.narration: ALONE BY THE FIRE, A LONG-SILENT BELL BEGAN TO RING BY ITSELF.

bubbles.text: Then every bell in the house rang out at once — and just as suddenly, stopped.

panels.scene: the bald pointed-nosed old man in a striped nightgown and nightcap clutching a wooden chair in terror as a heavy iron chain drags itself up a dark stairwell toward his door, link by link

teen.narration: SOMETHING HEAVY WAS DRAGGING UP THE STAIRS.

bubbles.text: Clank… clank… coming up the stairs, straight toward his door.

panels.scene: the see-through translucent ghost of Old Marley coming straight through a closed door: a gaunt old man's face, a white bandage tied up over the head and under the jaw, a grey pigtail, an old waistcoat, dragging a long heavy chain hung with cash-boxes, padlocks, keys and ledgers; the door is faintly visible through his transparent body

teen.narration: THE GHOST OF MARLEY WALKED IN — DRAGGING A DREADFUL CHAIN.

bubbles.text: His body was see-through. The chain was made of cash-boxes, keys, padlocks and heavy purses.

panels.scene: the bald clean-shaven old miser in a striped nightgown and nightcap cowering low beside a small fire burning in a brick fireplace, one hand raised in disbelief, a dim room; no lettering anywhere
panels.composition: single subject — Scrooge denies his eyes

teen.narration: SCROOGE TRIED TO LAUGH IT OFF.

bubbles.speaker: SCROOGE
bubbles.text: You're no ghost — you're just a bit of bad beef I ate for dinner!

panels.scene: the translucent ghost of Old Marley, gaunt stooped and thin, a white jaw-bandage tied over his head, a grey pigtail, an old waistcoat and knee-breeches, holding up a length of the heavy chain of cash-boxes and padlocks he is bound in, his sorrowful face lifted; the dim room faintly visible through him — an old thin man, never muscular
panels.composition: single subject — the chain he forged

bubbles.speaker: MARLEY
bubbles.text: I wear the chain I forged in life — link by link.

bubbles.speaker: MARLEY
bubbles.text: People were my business! Kindness, mercy and charity — THAT was my business.

panels.scene: the translucent ghost of Marley with his jaw-bandage and money-chain floating out through an open window into a night sky filled with other faint wandering phantom shapes, looking back over his shoulder in warning

teen.narration: MARLEY GAVE HIS WARNING AND JOINED THE PHANTOMS OF THE NIGHT.

bubbles.speaker: MARLEY
bubbles.text: You will be haunted by Three Spirits. Expect the first when the bell tolls One.

bubbles.speaker: MARLEY
bubbles.text: It is your one chance to escape my fate.
